claim: CodeCircuit maps line-level attribution graphs (transcoder-based) to predict code correctness; topological features beat black-box (MaxProb, PPL, entropy, energy) and gray-box (CoE) baselines on Python, Java, C++.
stance_target: L1/L4: internal-state correctness signals at line level, with causal intervention
scope_conditions: MBPP with translated Java/C++ task sets; Gemma-2-2B-it with a transcoder; Table 1
quoted_support: Topological features from these internal graphs predict correctness more reliably than surface heuristics and enable targeted causal interventions to fix erroneous logic.

breadth.confidence_families: MaxProb, PPL, entropy, temperature scaling, energy (black-box); CoE-R, CoE-C (gray-box); attribution-graph features (Sec 4.1, Table 1)
breadth.base_vs_instruct: not present (searched: full text, keyword scan)
breadth.post_training_stages: not present (searched: full text, keyword scan)
breadth.reasoning_models: not present (searched: full text, keyword scan)
breadth.elicitation_formats: not present (searched: full text, keyword scan)
breadth.calibration_metrics: AUROC, AUPR, FPR@95 (Sec 4.1, Table 1); no ECE
breadth.causal_intervention: yes: targeted node interventions to correct logic (Intro, Sec 4)
